stimulus.text: The engraving, 'The Bloody Massacre perpetrated in King-Street Boston on March 5th 1770,' was engraved, printed, and sold by Paul Revere. It shows a neat line of British soldiers firing a single volley into a crowd of Bostonians, with five men fallen in the foreground. Below the image, the names of the dead are listed: Samuel Gray, Samuel Maverick, James Caldwell, Crispus Attucks, and Patrick Carr — 'Killed. Six wounded.'
stimulus.source_note: Paul Revere, 1770. Library of Congress. Public domain (pre-1930).

books.section: A. Colonial Resistance to British Policies in the Aftermath of the French and Indian War
The Sugar Act, the Currency Act, and the Stamp Act

stem: According to the engraving's own caption, how many Bostonians were killed, and who was among them?

options.text: Five were killed, including Crispus Attucks
Eight were killed, including Samuel Adams
options.misconception: Eight was the number of soldiers tried, not killed — and Samuel Adams was not among the dead; he was the one who spread the news of the event.

options.text: Two were killed, including John Hancock
options.misconception: Two was the number of soldiers convicted, not killed — and Hancock was a merchant whose ship had been seized, not a victim of the shooting.

options.text: Six were killed, including Paul Revere
options.misconception: Six was the number wounded, not killed — and Revere engraved the scene; he was not shot in it.

rationales.A: The caption lists the dead by name: Samuel Gray, Samuel Maverick, James Caldwell, Crispus Attucks, and Patrick Carr — five killed, six wounded. Attucks, an African American, is named among them.
rationales.B: Eight were tried, not killed. Samuel Adams lived to spread the story; he was not a victim of it.
rationales.C: Two soldiers were convicted. Hancock was alive — his seized ship, not his death, is part of this story.
rationales.D: Six were wounded, not killed. Revere made the engraving; he was not shot in the street.
rationales.general:
1. Read the caption, not just the picture. It names the dead: Gray, Maverick, Caldwell, Attucks, and Carr — five names.
2. Note who is among them. Crispus Attucks, an African American, is listed with the rest, and the caption says six more were wounded.
3. Keep the numbers straight. Five killed, six wounded, eight soldiers tried — three different numbers for three different facts.
Remember: captions are evidence too — the words under a picture often carry the facts the picture cannot.
